s:
Consider the following statements.

s:
Which of the following statements are true about India?

I. India is the fifth largest country of the world.

II. It occupies about 2.4 per cent of the total area of the lithosphere.

IV. 82°30' East longitude is used to determine Indian Standard Time.

s: What is the Radcliffe line?
x: India has natural as well as man-made boundaries. The himalayas in the north, Bay of Bengal in the south-east, Indian Ocean in the south and Arabian Sea in the south-west form its natural boundary. s:

x: Under the so-called China- Pakistan 'Boundary Agreement' signed in 1963, Pakistan illegally ceded 5180 sq. km of territory in Shaksgam Valley (part of the Union Territory of Ladakh) to China. x: Palk Strait The Palk Strait separates the southeastern coast of India from northern Sri Lanka. It lies between Tamil Nadu and the Jaffna peninsula. Travellers from Nagercoil towards Sri Lanka would cross this strait.

s: Sri Lanka is separated from India by the
x: Sri Lanka is separated from mainland India by the Gulf of Mannar and the Palk Strait, a shallow sea passage between the two countries. This stretch is also known for Adam's Bridge, a chain of limestone shoals connecting the two landmasses. The strait has historical, ecological, and maritime significance.

s: The Palk Bay lies between:
o: Gulf of Kachchh and Gulf of Khambhat
Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal
x: Palk Bay is an inlet of the Bay of Bengal located between India and Sri Lanka. It is bounded in the south by Adam's Bridge and connects to the Bay of Bengal through the Palk Strait. Geographically, it is linked to the adjoining Gulf of Mannar to the southwest. Hence, Palk Bay forms the marine stretch between the Bay of Bengal and the Gulf of Mannar along the India–Sri Lanka maritime boundary.

s: Which one of the following pairs of islands is separated from each other by the 'Ten Degree Channel'?

s: Out of the four southern states – Andhra Pradesh Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, which shares boundaries with maximum number of Indian states?
o: Each of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka
Each of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
x: Option (c) was correct when this question was asked. After the reorganization of Andhra Pradesh, the scenario of States and their borders is as follows – Andhra Pradesh borders with Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. If the Yaman region of Pondicherry (now Puducherry) is also taken into consideration the number of States/Union Territories bordering Andhra Pradesh will be six. Karnataka shares boundaries with six states – Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Goa, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Kerala shares border with 2 States – Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. If the Mahe region of Pondicherry (now Puducherry) is included the number of States/Union Territories bordering Kerala will be three. Tamil Nadu shares border with three states-Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and including Pondicherry (now Puducherry), the number of States/Union Territories will be four. Telangana borders with Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Thus, presently, Karnataka shares a border with the maximum number of states.
